title: Connected affine algebraic groups of dimension at most two are solvable
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $\dim G$ be the Krull dimension of its underlying topological space [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $\dim G\leq2$, then $G$ is solvable in the scheme-theoretic derived-series sense [def-sfb-semisimple-group-scheme]: there is an integer $n\geq0$ for which $D^nG=1$, where $D^0G=G$ and $D^{a+1}G$ is the smallest closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] of $D^aG$ through which its commutator morphism factors. No restriction on the characteristic of $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Corollary 17.27, printed p.360, with the standing hypotheses of Section 17b on printed p.353 (connected group variety over an algebraically closed field); group variety equals smooth algebraic group by Proposition 1.26, printed p.13. Solvability is the scheme-theoretic derived-series notion of Proposition 6.30, printed p.132.

proof.text: Choose a smooth connected solvable closed subgroup $B\subseteq G$ of greatest dimension. Such subgroups exist (the identity subgroup is one), and their dimensions are nonnegative integers bounded by $\dim G$ by [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products]. That same node says every proper inclusion of smooth connected groups strictly increases dimension. Consequently no larger smooth connected solvable subgroup contains $B$, so $B$ is Borel by [def-sfb-borel-subgroup-scheme]. Put $d=\dim B$; then $0\leq d\leq2$. If $d=2$, a proper inclusion $B\subsetneq G$ would give $2<\dim G$, a contradiction. Thus $B=G$ in this case, proving solvability.

source.place: Corollary 17.27, printed p.360, choice of B and dimension-two case; largest-dimension observation following Definition 17.6, printed pp.353--354.

proof.text: For $d\leq1$, apply [lem-sfb-perfect-solvable-unipotent-torus] to $B$. Its solvability hypothesis (a normal series with commutative quotients) holds for the derived series $D^aB$: for every algebra $A$, $D^{a+1}B(A)$ contains all commutators of $D^aB(A)$, so $hxh^{-1}=[h,x]x$ shows that $D^{a+1}B$ is normal in $D^aB$, and commutators of local sections of $D^aB/D^{a+1}B$ lift locally to commutators lying in the kernel $D^{a+1}B$ of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], so the quotients are commutative. The base $k$ is perfect because an algebraically closed field has no proper algebraic extensions. We obtain a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup $U\subseteq B$ and a torus quotient $D=B/U$. By [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], the quotient is represented by an affine finite-type group, its map $q:B\to D$ is faithfully flat of finite presentation, its kernel is $U$, and $B\times_D B\simeq B\times_k U$. These are the represented coset quotient properties. The group $B$ is separated by [lem-sc-group-scheme-separated-field], so [lem-sfb-homogeneous-quotient-krull-dimension] applies and gives $d=\dim U+\dim D$. In particular one of $U,D$ has dimension zero.

source.place: Corollary 17.27 and Theorem 16.33(a)--(c), printed pp.335--336; Proposition 5.23, printed p.104. The split uses the quotient version of the same unipotent/torus dichotomy.

proof.text: A smooth connected dimension-zero group $H$ here is trivial: if $1\subsetneq H$, [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products] gives $0\leq\dim1<\dim H=0$, impossible. Thus either $U=1$ or $D=1$. If $D=1$, the kernel equality in the previous step gives $B=U$. If $U=1$, the torsor identity makes $q$ a monomorphism: any two local lifts differ by a section of $U$, hence agree. Every section of $D$ has an fppf-local lift to $B$; uniqueness makes these lifts agree on overlaps and glue. Thus $q$ is an isomorphism of represented sheaves, and hence of group schemes, so $B\simeq D$. We have obtained that $B$ is either unipotent or a torus, including the trivial case.

source.place: Corollary 17.27, printed p.360, cases dim B=0,1; quotient-kernel and sheaf argument for Theorem 16.33 decomposition.

proof.text: If $B$ is unipotent, [lem-sfb-perfect-unipotent-additive-series] gives a finite descending series $B=B_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq B_m=1$ with $B_i/B_{i+1}$ central in $B/B_{i+1}$. Since the kernel of $B\to B/B_{i+1}$ is $B_{i+1}$ and $B_i/B_{i+1}$ is the image of $B_i$ in $B/B_{i+1}$ [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], centrality says exactly that $[B(A),B_i(A)]\subseteq B_{i+1}(A)$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$, so this is the nilpotent series required by [lem-sfb-nilpotent-borel-equals-group]. If $B$ is a torus, it is isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$; multiplication is commutative on every algebra by [def-sc-gm-ga], and $B\supseteq1$ is such a series. In either case the nilpotent-Borel criterion gives $G=B$. Since $B$ was chosen solvable, the derived series of $G$ terminates. All three possible values of $d$ are covered, in every characteristic.

source.place: Corollary 17.27, printed p.360; Proposition 17.23(b) to (c), printed p.359; Corollary 16.24, printed p.331, for the unipotent central series.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q148-400b248cb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read Milne iAG2017 pp.358-360: Prop. 17.21-17.23 with proofs and Cor. 17.27. The item statement matches 17.27 (k algebraically closed; G smooth, connected and affine of finite type; dim<=2; scheme-theoretic derived-series solvability; any characteristic), and the 4-step route follows Milne's proof. Step 1: taking B of greatest dimension makes it a Borel, using the strict-growth and dimension-bound clause of solvable-normal-subgroup-products; dim B=2 forces G=B. Step 2: B/U is a torus by perfect-solvable-unipotent-torus; by affine-normal-quotient-geometry it has kernel U and B×U≅B×_D B, so B/U is the coset quotient; 047L (Lean-closed slopmaster2 GrpObj.isSeparated_hom) gives separatedness; homogeneous-quotient-krull-dimension gives d=dim U+dim D. Step 3: a smooth connected zero-dimensional group is trivial by strict growth (smoothness excludes alpha_p); a mono that is also an fppf epi is an isomorphism. Step 4: the central additive series becomes commutator containment; a torus is commutative; the new criterion gives G=B. New node lem-sfb-nilpotent-borel-equals-group is Milne 17.23 (b)=>(c) in the G=B form proved there. Its objects are introduced in the node and it is statement-only. Tested on the trivial group, Ga, Gm, Ga⋊Gm (Borel = G, not nilpotent, so nothing claimed) and SL2 (Borel not nilpotent). It is not a clause of the item. No duplicate: checked central-maximal-torus-nilpotent (17.23 (d)=>(c)), nilpotent-connected-central-series, borel-scheme-normalizer, general-borel-flag-variety (circular via 17.27) and the main-20261015 blueprint. No cycle; the item is unsplit live and side-live; no SGA. Batch-5: the trf nodes reached are generic Mathlib leaves (fppf covering base change, fpqc smooth descent) and definitions (descent datum, scheme as algebraic space), not trace-formula or Poincaré steps, so they are accepted.
